candidates.title: Review missing store purchase information

demandEvidence.chore: Review a public storefront and list which buyer-confidence details—reviews, policies, contact details or business background—appear missing.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: Is there any missing information—such as reviews, policies, contact details, or business background—that would make you hesitate to buy?

ease.reason: A student can manually test a checklist against a public or fictional storefront; no supplied reference supports automated site review.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: small online shop owners may value a structured storefront review; this single question proves no buyer or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week mock can produce a checklist from supplied page text, but review criteria and useful accuracy are unvalidated.

autonomy.reason: A draft checklist can repeat from supplied page text; a person must verify omissions and avoid treating absence as fact.

evidence.reason: The question names reviews, policies, contact details and business background, but gives no repeat-use evidence or rubric.

candidates.reason: Below threshold (4.6 mean). A test checklist is possible, but the single feedback question and lack of implementation evidence do not support an effective repeatable AI service.

candidates.title: Capture checkout instructions as an order note

demandEvidence.chore: Let a shopper enter special instructions or a custom message before checkout.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: I want to allow customers to add special instructions or custom messages before they proceed to checkout.

ease.reason: A mock form can collect a test message, but no supplied reference supports Shopify checkout changes.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: some merchants may value capturing order instructions; this feature request establishes no AI-service buyer or payment.

feasibility.reason: A synthetic form can demonstrate capture in four weeks; actual checkout integration and platform constraints are unsupported.

autonomy.reason: A form could capture repeated messages, while a merchant must interpret requests and confirm order handling.

evidence.reason: The request clearly identifies pre-checkout messages, but says nothing about frequency, validation or implementation.

candidates.reason: Below threshold (4.2 mean). Capturing a note is a bounded feature request, but adding AI offers no supported benefit and the supplied evidence does not establish an AI workflow or implementation.

candidates.title: Update variant unit prices in a storefront

demandEvidence.chore: Update the displayed unit price when a shopper selects a different product variant.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: I’m customizing the Dawn theme and looking for a way to update the unit price dynamically via JavaScript when a customer selects a different product variant.

ease.reason: A sample page could demonstrate a price refresh, but the request names JavaScript theme work and no reference supports its mechanics.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: merchants may value correct variant pricing; this one implementation question proves neither repeat demand nor AI-service payment.

feasibility.reason: A sample-data prototype is conceivable, but actual theme behavior, price rules and integration are unspecified.

autonomy.reason: A browser can refresh a displayed value after selection; a person must verify price rules and live storefront behavior.

evidence.reason: The post names variant selection and dynamic unit-price display, but supplies no formula, sample or corroboration.

candidates.reason: Below threshold (4.0 mean). The task is concrete but looks like a one-off theme customization; no supplied implementation evidence supports a useful AI service.
